one_line_summary: An arts education program for youth in Los Angeles, providing a summer arts camp with enrichment programming.
mission: To provide youth with the tools to create, connect, and heal through art, wellness, and community.

programs.name: Summer Arts Camp
programs.description: Immersive workshops in visual arts, music production, dance, and creative entrepreneurship, led by industry professionals.
programs.population_served: Youth ages 12-18 from underserved Los Angeles-area communities; the 2025 camp aimed to engage 100 youth, with a focus on accessibility, diversity, and empowerment.
programs.site_model: Satellite site model, hosted with SJLI (Social Justice Learning Institute), 600 Centinela Blvd, Inglewood, CA. The 2025 camp ran weekly (Wednesdays, June 11-July 2) at this site. REPLACE ME: confirm current MOU status for future years.

org_status.fiscal_sponsor_or_501c3: Not yet incorporated as a 501(c)(3) and no fiscal sponsor in place (as of Sept 2026). This is the top-priority gap to close: most foundation and federal grants (NEA, LA County Arts Commission, Adobe, Disney included) require one or the other before they'll even accept an application. Options worth evaluating: file for 501(c)(3) directly, or apply for fiscal sponsorship through an existing nonprofit (e.g. Fractured Atlas or Fulcrum Arts both run arts-focused fiscal sponsorship programs open to individuals/projects, or ask SJLI directly whether they'd sponsor given the existing camp partnership) - verify current eligibility/fees with each before committing.
